newsitem.title: THAILAND: Ailing Thai bank to recall loans via stocks sales.
newsitem.headline: Ailing Thai bank to recall loans via stocks sales.

text.p: Thailand's troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc plans to sell shares in five listed companies as part of its attempt to recall a portion of its bad loans, a bank official said on Wednesday.
The shares to be sold were put as collateral by Bangkok Bank of Commerce's borrowers to secure funds for acquisitions of those companies, the bank's vice president Sondhaya Noicharoen told reporters.
"We expect to receive about five billion baht from the sale of those shares," Sondhaya said.
The shares to be sold would be from Semiconductor Ventures International Plc, Interlife Assurance Plc, Phuket Island Plc, Phoenix Pulp and Paper Plc and Precious Shipping Plc, he said.

The government took over the ailing bank in May 1996 to save it from a massive run on its deposits after it was found to have huge bad loans. The semi-government Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand has been appointed to manage the bank as well as take a stake in it.
The bank said it has been saddled with net non-performing loans, after collateral deduction, valued at 53.78 billion baht ($2.07 billion) at end-1996.
It also posted a huge 24.8 billion baht net loss in 1996 against an 860.4 million profit in 1995.
